title: Little Hawley Rising Anew
premise: Retired detective Kestrel Thornbury, drowning in the debts of their failing bookshop, is handed the diary of Marlowe Vane, a woman who vanished from Little Hawley eleven years ago. The diary's final entries are dated after her disappearance, written in a hand that grows shakier with each page, and they name a witness everyone in town insists died years before. As Kestrel follows the diary's trail, they uncover that Marlowe faked her death to escape a powerful local family and has been hiding in plain sight ever since, while the 'dead' witness is being hunted by someone desperate to bury an old crime. In the climax at the flooded quarry, Kestrel must choose between protecting Marlowe's fragile new life and exposing the truth that will save the witness, ending with Kestrel closing the case on their own terms: publishing the truth as a novel in their shop window while Marlowe walks free.
about_author: Xanthe Blackwood is the pen name of a former small-town archivist who spent a decade cataloguing unsolved cases in county records. They write mysteries where the past refuses to stay filed away.

chapters.title: The Diary That Outlived Her
chapters.summary: Kestrel Thornbury, POV. A grieving stranger leaves Marlowe Vane's diary on the bookshop counter; its entries continue past the date she vanished. Kestrel, broke and restless, begins reading against their better judgment. The emotional beat is reluctant fascination — the detective's old hunger stirring in a life gone stale.

chapters.title: Everyone Swears She's Dead
chapters.summary: Kestrel POV. Interviews in Little Hawley reveal a town rehearsed in grief: the Ashcombe family, the vicar, the pub landlord all repeat the same story too smoothly. But the diary names a witness — Ida Fenwick — whose gravestone Kestrel finds suspiciously pristine. Emotional beat: mounting unease as loyalty and lies blur.

chapters.title: What the Quarry Keeps
chapters.summary: Kestrel POV, intercut with diary excerpts. Following the shaky late entries to the flooded quarry, Kestrel discovers Ida alive, hidden by Marlowe herself, and learns the Ashcombes caused a death the town agreed to forget. Someone burns the bookshop's back room in warning. Emotional beat: terror sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: A Case Worth Closing
chapters.summary: Kestrel POV. Confronted at the quarry by the last living Ashcombe, Kestrel trades silence for evidence, forcing a confession recorded by Ida. Marlowe surrenders her anonymity only long enough to testify, then vanishes again — leaving Kestrel one final diary entry thanking them. Emotional beat: bittersweet closure, truth chosen over safety.
